title: Trace failure to a completed checkpoint
description: Move the failure against periodic snapshots, then choose the sink boundary. The model exposes which input span is replayed and when replay can leak into duplicate business effects.

profiles.label: Healthy snapshots
profiles.detail: Snapshots finish well before the next trigger and the failure lands between checkpoints.

profiles.label: Large state snapshot
profiles.detail: A longer snapshot leaves more time in which the newest trigger has not completed.

profiles.label: Failure during snapshot
profiles.detail: The active checkpoint is incomplete, so recovery falls back to the previous completed barrier.

sinkModes.label: Checkpoint-aware transactional sink
sinkModes.detail: Output commits participate in the checkpoint protocol.
sinkModes.consequence: Flink reprocesses the replay span, while transactions associated with incomplete checkpoints remain uncommitted. Source, managed state, and supported sink output can present one consistent result after recovery.

sinkModes.label: Idempotent external sink
sinkModes.detail: A stable business key turns repeated attempts into the same logical write.
sinkModes.consequence: Replay can issue the write again, but the destination recognizes the operation key and preserves one logical effect. This is an application contract that must be tested; Flink cannot infer it.

sinkModes.label: Uncoordinated side effect
sinkModes.detail: The sink commits immediately and has no transaction or deduplication key.
sinkModes.consequence: A record processed after the restore point may execute its external effect again during replay. Exactly-once managed state does not make an arbitrary HTTP call, email, or payment exactly once.
